summary: A public sale still prices on a reseller's channel while consuming public stock (TKT-246 residual)

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — HOLD AT GATE 1 (one human decision)

Shaped 2026-08-17. Seven of eight DoR items **met**; `approach` is **open with `owner: human`**,
deliberately.

#### Why this one may not use the escape hatch

`shaping.md` carves out exactly this case: `approach: deferred` does **not** pass when a ticket
touches auth or money paths. This is both. Deferring would move a trust-boundary call from shaping —
where there is time to read and a human to ask — into Planning under a drafting deadline.

#### The finding that changes the ticket's severity

The ticket describes the residual as *"a **fee-attribution** defect, not an inventory-theft one"*.
Reading `ADR-046 §3` upgrades that:

> `passed_on` — added to what the buyer is charged. `absorbed` — borne by the organizer out of the
> face value. **Incidence is not a display flag.**

So a public buyer naming a reseller channel whose rules are `absorbed` **is charged less**, and the
organizer eats the difference. That is a **revenue leak**, not a reporting artifact. It does not
change the non-goals, but it does change how option (C) reads.

#### The decision (yours)

| | shape | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | public callers may name **no** channel; the field becomes partner-only | breaks any public presale/affiliate flow that legitimately prices on a channel without a partner credential |
| **B** | a channel **opts in** to being publicly nameable — catalog's analogue of ADR-024's `sold_by` | a migration + a registry field |
| **C** | accept and argue it — the COS explicitly permits "any string" *if argued* | shaping's read: now the **weakest**, because the leak is money, not metadata. Recorded so it is rejected knowingly rather than by omission |

#### The ticket's proposed remedy, verified rather than inherited

It suggests *"channel-scoped fee rules require the same authorization inventory now requires"*.
**That does not transfer cleanly**, and saying so is worth more than repeating it: inventory's guard
is judged **under the pool row lock** (ADR-024) because it is an *accounting* decision. Fee
resolution has no lock and no such row — it is a pure read on a **public** endpoint whose contract
already documents deliberate non-disclosure of other channels' rules. The remedy is an
**eligibility rule at resolve time**, not a copy of inventory's row-lock check.

#### The test that must not be inverted

`services/commerce/internal/api/channel_seam_test.go` is a live tripwire that says, in its own
comment, not to delete it. It pins the public GA hold as channel-free. **This ticket must not invert
it** — the inventory half is TKT-246's closed decision. A plan that "fixes" this by forwarding the
channel will fail there loudly, which is the tripwire working.

**Stale pointer found while reading it:** its closing comment says *"See TKT-247 for the
remainder"*. TKT-247 is a scanner-device flake. The remainder is **this ticket**. Correct that
comment as part of this work.

#### And the assertion that makes COS 3 bite

The COS asks for "a test that executes a public sale naming a reseller channel and asserts the
resulting fee basis". Shaping adds: it must assert the **fee basis *and* the amount charged**, not
merely that the call was refused. Under `incidence=absorbed` the defect shows up as a *smaller
charge*; a refusal-only assertion is structurally blind to it. Derive the expected value from the
requirement, never from a run.

#### Registry defect noticed in passing

**ADR-055 is a duplicated number** — both `ADR-055-presale-unlock-codes.md` and
`ADR-055-on-sale-write-rate-limiting.md` exist. Cite by filename, not by number. Not this ticket's
to fix; flagged for the owner.

**Verdict: NOT READY — one human decision (A / B / C) stands between this and Gate 1.**
Everything else is prepared; answer in the thread and the agent records it and flips `approach`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Readiness UPDATE — Gate 1 decision taken by the owner

`approach` flips **open → met**. All eight DoR items now met; no open blockers.

#### The decision: option A

**Public callers may name no channel.** `channel_code` becomes partner-only — taken from the
credential, never from a body, which is what the partner path already does
(`server.go:620-636`). A public request that still sends the field gets a **400**: the contract
refuses it *and* the handler refuses it, mirroring the existing comment's reasoning — the guard must
not depend on the contract never being edited.

Verified before recommending it, so A's stated cost turns out not to apply here: **no public product
flow prices on a channel today.** The storefront never sends `channel_code` (`grep` over `web/`
returns nothing outside generated types). The only public callers that name one are tests.

#### The complication I raised, and how it was resolved

`smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go` asserts a public sale on an *unregistered* channel completes
end to end, and its header instructs the reader that overturning it requires saying why in the
commit. Two different questions were hiding behind one field:

| question | answer | owner |
|---|---|---|
| Is the code **registered**? | Don't gate on it — retired channels must keep selling so historical attribution survives | ADR-024 / TKT-235 / TKT-241 — **untouched** |
| Is the caller **entitled** to price on it? | No, unless authenticated | **this ticket** |

A answers only the second. Because the public path stops accepting the field entirely, **no registry
lookup is ever added** — the registry remains a lookup, not a constraint. The partner half of that
file is unchanged and keeps proving an unregistered code sells verbatim. Only the public half
narrows, and not because the rule changed: because a public sale can no longer name a channel at all.

That distinction is what the ticket's ADR must say explicitly, or the next reader will record this
as ADR-024 having been overturned when it was not.

#### Carried forward into implementation

- The test must assert the **fee basis and the amount charged**, not just a refusal — under
  `incidence=absorbed` the defect is a *smaller* charge, and a refusal-only assertion is blind to it.
- `channel_seam_test.go` must **not** invert; its stale "See TKT-247" pointer gets corrected to
  TKT-248.
- The ticket text's proposed remedy (copy inventory's authorization) does not transfer — inventory
  judges under the pool row lock because it is an accounting decision; this is an eligibility rule
  on a lockless public read.

**Verdict: READY.** Gate 1 cleared by the owner.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-248

Running **gateless per `config.gates: autonomous`** for gates 2–4. **Gate 1 was taken by the owner**
(option A, plus two follow-up decisions on scope and refusal shape) — not self-promoted.

**Backend:** local tracker. **Branch:** `TKT-248-partner-only-channel-pricing` off `origin/main`
(`2e8d9e1c`).

**Selection reason:** the owner named it, and it is the recorded residual of TKT-246 — the half that
was deliberately left open so it would be a decision rather than an oversight. Shaping upgraded its
severity from fee mis-attribution to a **revenue leak** (ADR-046 §3: an `absorbed` fee on a channel
a public buyer names is borne by the organizer, so the buyer is charged less).

**Blockers:** none open. TKT-246 (Done) is the parent decision; TKT-240 (reverted) is the
cautionary precedent.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` is NOT claimed.** Stated explicitly rather than left silent. This is an
**authorization change on a money path** — two of the label's carve-outs at once — and it edits a
public API contract. The plan gate stays, and the plan is drafted by a second model.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — by `gpt-5.6-luna` (config.models.plan), via the codex companion, read-only

Briefed with the ticket, the owner's Gate 1 decision (option A + 400 + registry-untouched), the
governing ADRs, the governing tests, and the AGENTS.md rules that bite here. Told the decision was
made and not to re-open it. Asked to challenge the facts it was given.

**Facts the orchestrator verified before briefing** (executed, so the drafter did not have to
re-derive them): no public product flow prices on a channel (`grep` over `web/` is empty outside
generated types); the partner path already takes the channel from its credential
(`server.go:620-636`); `ReservationCreate` already carries `additionalProperties: false`; and
`PartnerReservationCreate` already models "the guard is the absence of the field, not a check".

**Two facts the orchestrator found that the ticket text does not mention**, both handed to the
drafter: the leak has **two arms, not one** — `channel_code` feeds `resolveTicketTypePrice`
(`server.go:796`) as well as `resolveTicketTypeFees` (`server.go:810`), and TKT-237 gave price rules
the channel axis, so a public caller can move the **base price**, not just the fees.

---

# TKT-248 execution plan

No files were modified. The worktree is clean on `TKT-248-partner-only-channel-pricing`.

## 1. Mechanism

Implement both contract- and handler-level refusal.

1. In `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml:643-706`:

   - Remove `channel_code` from `ReservationCreate.properties`.
   - Change `maxProperties` from `4` to `3`.
   - Update the description to state that public reservations are channel-free.
   - Keep `additionalProperties: false`.
   - Leave `PartnerReservationCreate` unchanged; its existing “absence is the guard” model is the precedent.

   This makes a public body containing `channel_code`, including `channel_code: ""`, fail contract validation with `400` before the handler runs. Schema-only enforcement is insufficient because the handler could later be reached with an edited contract or direct invocation.

2. In `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:351-382,610-639`, retain the internal `reserveRequest.ChannelCode` pointer as a defense-in-depth tripwire, but add:

   - For `scope == nil`, reject any non-`nil` `ChannelCode` with `400`.
   - Perform this immediately after decoding and before pricing, fee resolution, persistence, or inventory.
   - For a partner scope, preserve the existing overwrite at lines 630-635: the credential remains the only accepted channel authority.

   Do not silently clear the public field. The schema makes the field unsubmittable; the handler check ensures a future contract edit cannot turn it into a trusted public input.

## 2. Plumbing and persistence

For a new public reservation, `in.ChannelCode` becomes `nil`:

- Price resolution: `server.go:796` → `catalog_pricing.go:93-103`.
- Fee resolution: `server.go:810-811` → `catalog_fees.go:268-276`.
- Both catalog requests omit `channel_code`, selecting ADR-046’s default/public context.
- `reservations.channel_code` remains nullable and is written as `NULL` at `server.go:975-976`.
- `reservations.reseller_id` remains `NULL` for public sales.
- `fee_resolution_snapshot` is still persisted for fee-enabled public sales. Its embedded resolution must contain `"channel_code": null`; absorbed fees remain in the snapshot but are excluded from the buyer’s total because `composedTotal` adds only passed-on fees (`catalog_fees.go:409-418`).
- Checkout continues copying `reservations.channel_code` and `reseller_id` into `orders` at `server.go:1239-1244`.

The columns must not be removed or backfilled. They are required for:

- Historical partner attribution.
- Historical public rows created before TKT-248.
- Settlement and exchange behavior.
- The existing database constraints in migrations `0014_fee_composition.sql:121-125` and `0020_reseller_credentials.sql:90-104`.

The partner path remains:

- Credential scope is applied at `server.go:620-635`.
- `addSellerScope` sends the credential channel and reseller to inventory at `server.go:519-545`.
- Catalog pricing and fee resolution receive the credential channel.
- Reservation, order, claim, and fee snapshot rows retain the channel.

## 3. Legacy rows and replay compatibility

The phrase “public channel is always `NULL`” applies to new public writes, not historical data. Existing rows can legally have:

```text
reservations.channel_code IS NOT NULL
reservations.reseller_id IS NULL
```

That state is explicitly exercised by `exchange_target_test.go:104-123` and `exchange_attribution_smoke_test.go:105-117`.

The replay path currently reads the stored channel at `server.go:663-665` and compares it through `sameTerms` / `sameChannel` (`catalog_fees.go:507-555`). A retry of an old public reservation, now omitting `channel_code`, would otherwise become a `409` because `nil` differs from the stored channel.

Preserve compatibility by adding a narrowly scoped legacy-public replay exception:

- A new submitted channel still receives `400`.
- A channel-less public retry may replay an existing row only when `reseller_id IS NULL` and the row predates this policy.
- Replay must return the persisted amount and fee snapshot; it must not re-resolve fees.
- Partner rows and current channel-term comparisons remain exact.

Add a fixture that directly seeds the legacy state and proves the replay path. Do not create it through the current public API, since that would make the precondition unreachable.

## 4. Test plan and non-vacuity

| Test | Assertion | Edit that must make it red |
|---|---|---|
| Contract test in `catalog_fees_test.go:421` | Public GA/seated bodies without a channel remain valid; bodies containing `channel_code` are invalid. | Re-add `channel_code` to `ReservationCreate`, or leave the old property ceiling. |
| Public handler refusal, replacing `TestAChannelledGASaleDoesNotYetForwardItsChannel` at `channel_seam_test.go:114` | A public GA request naming `reseller-acme` returns `400`; catalog and inventory are not called. | Delete the handler guard at `server.go` and the request proceeds. |
| Public no-channel seam, existing `channel_seam_test.go:138-165` | A legitimate public GA sale still reaches inventory without a `channel` field. | Add any public `addSellerScope` channel forward. |
| Public fee integration test | Seed a channel-agnostic `per_ticket_fixed`, `passed_on` rule and a channel-specific `per_ticket_fixed`, `absorbed` rule. A channel-less public sale must assert the public rule’s basis, incidence, fee amount, `passed_on_fees`, and exact gross charge. Persisted reservation/order channel columns must be `NULL`. | Remove fee resolution, inject a channel, treat absorbed fees as passed-on, or charge the wrong total. |
| Partner fee integration test | The credential channel reaches catalog; the partner snapshot records the channel-specific basis/incidence/amount; the gross charge matches the absorbed-fee rule; inventory still receives credential channel and reseller. | Stop overwriting from scope, omit the catalog query parameter, or remove either inventory identity field. |
| Legacy replay test | A directly seeded historical public-channel row replays through a channel-less request using its stored amount/snapshot. | Remove the compatibility branch or accidentally re-resolve current fees. |
| Existing `TestSameTermsComparesEveryIdempotencyTerm` at `catalog_fees_test.go:752` | Current channel terms remain distinct for partner/current rows. | Remove channel comparison from `sameTerms`. |
| Exchange tests at `exchange_target_test.go:104-123` | Public legacy source sends neither channel nor reseller to inventory. | Make `holdExchangeTarget` forward a historical public channel. |

For the money fixture, derive all expected values from named fixture constants. Do not copy numbers observed from a run. The absorbed-fee case is essential: a refusal-only test cannot detect the original revenue leak, where the buyer paid less and the organizer absorbed the difference.

## 5. Narrowing the registry smoke test

Change `smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go:388-463`:

- Rename `TestAPublicSaleOnAnUnregisteredChannelCompletesEndToEnd` to reflect the new refusal/no-channel boundary.
- Remove its old successful reservation, checkout, fee, split, and attribution assertions.
- Do not retain registry or fee seeds that cannot affect a request rejected before catalog; they would be decorative fixtures.
- Assert that a public request containing a channel is refused.
- Keep `TestAPartnerSaleOnAnUnregisteredChannelCompletesEndToEnd` at `:465-539` unchanged. It remains the end-to-end proof that an unregistered credential channel sells verbatim.

Update the file header with this exact rationale:

> Under TKT-248, public reservations may not name a channel; the public half is therefore narrowed to the refusal boundary, while the partner half remains the end-to-end proof that an unregistered credential channel sells verbatim. ADR-024’s registry-as-lookup decision is unchanged.

The commit message must carry the same explanation.

## 6. ADR

Use the next free number: `ADR-060`.

Proposed file and title:

```text
docs/adr/ADR-060-public-reservation-channel-entitlement.md
# ADR-060: Public reservations cannot name partner channels
```

The ADR must state:

- Public reservations have no caller-supplied channel.
- Public requests containing the field receive `400`.
- Partner channels come only from the authenticated ADR-056 credential.
- New public reservations persist `NULL` channel attribution.
- Historical rows remain immutable and retain their snapshots/attribution.
- This is an entitlement/authorization decision, not a registry decision.
- **ADR-024 is not overturned:** the channel registry remains a lookup, not a sale constraint; unregistered and retired channels continue to work for authenticated partner credentials.
- The relevant duplicated-number reference is specifically `ADR-055-presale-unlock-codes.md`, not the rate-limiting ADR.

## 7. Regeneration and gate

After changing the commerce OpenAPI document:

1. Run `make generate`.
2. Verify the commerce generated model loses `ReservationCreate.ChannelCode` at `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go:574-580`.
3. Verify the storefront generated type loses `channel_code` at `web/storefront/src/lib/commerce-api-types.gen.ts:433-445`.
4. Commit regenerated files before running the gate, because `check-generate` diffs against `HEAD`.
5. Run focused commerce tests.
6. Run `make check`.

`make browser` is not required: this ticket changes no storefront or back-office write form.

## 8. Exchange risk

The exchange path does reprice the target with the source channel:

- `exchanges.go:143-145` passes `src.ChannelCode` to price resolution.
- It does not perform a fresh fee resolution; the prior fee is carried through the exchange gross calculation.
- `holdExchangeTarget` only sends channel and reseller to inventory when both `src.ResellerID` and `src.ChannelCode` are present (`exchanges.go:363-420`).
- The replacement reservation and order copy attribution from the source (`exchanges.go:575-635`).

Do not weaken the partner exchange behavior. New public rows have no channel, so new public exchanges remain public. Historical public-channel rows remain a compatibility edge: they may still reprice from historical channel data while correctly avoiding channel-authorized inventory consumption. Document and test that behavior rather than silently changing historical exchange economics in TKT-248.

## 9. Corrections to stale repository text

The brief is substantively correct. Two repository comments are stale and should be corrected while touching the seam:

- `services/commerce/internal/api/channel_seam_test.go:54` says “See TKT-247 for the remainder”; it should point to TKT-248.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:535-538` labels the residual as TKT-247; it should identify TKT-248.

The OpenAPI and `reserveRequest` comments also currently describe public channel pricing as an open TKT-246 defect (`openapi.yaml:671-706`, `server.go:361-381`); update them to describe the new public/partner split.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Plan critique — by `main-agent` (config.models.planReview)

Cross-model invariant holds: drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`, critiqued by `main-agent`. Every file, line
and symbol the draft cites was checked at HEAD. **It hallucinated nothing**, and it found two things
I had missed. Verifications I ran:

| draft claim | verdict |
|---|---|
| `ReservationCreate` has `maxProperties: 4`, must become `3` | ✅ `openapi.yaml:661` — and the `not:` block at :666 must stay |
| `sameChannel` would 409 a channel-less retry of a stored-channel row | ✅ `catalog_fees.go:547`, replay reads `channel_code` at `server.go:663` |
| ADR-060 is the next free number | ✅ `docs/adr/` ends at ADR-059 |
| a **second** stale TKT-247 pointer at `server.go:535-538` | ✅ confirmed — I had only found the one in `channel_seam_test.go` |
| exchange forwards only when `src.ResellerID != nil` | ✅ `exchanges.go:399` |

#### ACCEPT — the mechanism (§1), with the reasoning sharpened

Schema removal **and** a handler refusal. Correct, and it is the AGENTS.md *make-it-unsubmittable*
rule applied properly: the schema deletion is the real guard (the field stops existing), the handler
check is the second line for the day the contract is edited — exactly the reasoning already written
at `server.go:630` for the partner path. Note the generated struct field disappears, so the handler
check needs a decode path that can still *see* an unexpected key; say how in the plan rather than
discovering it at implementation time.

#### ACCEPT — §2 plumbing, §5 test narrowing, §6 ADR, §9 stale text

§5's proposed header sentence and §6's "ADR-024 is not overturned" clause are precisely what the
owner's decision requires. §9 catches the second stale pointer.

#### AMEND 1 (material) — §3's legacy-replay branch is the wrong shape for the risk

This is the draft's best find and its weakest remedy. The problem is real: an old public row with a
channel, retried without one, hits `sameChannel(stored, nil)` and 409s.

But the proposed fix — a permanent "legacy public replay" exception on a **money path**, with a
predicate meaning "the row predates this policy" — is worse than the problem:

1. **"Predates this policy" is not expressible.** There is no policy-version column. It would have
   to be inferred from `channel_code IS NOT NULL AND reseller_id IS NULL`, which is *also* the shape
   of a legitimate historical partner-era row and, per `exchange_target_test.go:106`, a "legal and
   routine" state. The predicate cannot distinguish what it claims to.
2. **It is a permanent branch for a transient condition**, on the path that decides what a buyer is
   charged on replay.
3. **The blast radius of not fixing it is one 409** on a retry of a reservation that (a) was created
   before this change, (b) named a channel, and (c) is being retried with the same idempotency key.
   A 409 here is *safe* — it refuses rather than mischarging — and the caller's remedy is a new key.

**Amendment:** do **not** add the branch. Instead: keep `sameChannel` exact, and **assert the 409
deliberately in a test** with a comment naming it as accepted behaviour — the ADR-021 idiom of
pinning a known gap as a test so the claim cannot drift from the behaviour. The ADR records it as a
consequence. If it ever bites a real integrator, that is a ticket with evidence, not a speculative
branch on a money path today.

#### AMEND 2 — §4's fixture must satisfy the money assertion the COS asks for

The draft's fee-integration row is right to seed a channel-agnostic `passed_on` rule **and** a
channel-specific `absorbed` rule. Two additions, both from AGENTS.md:

- **Of each seed, ask what deleting it turns red.** The absorbed rule is the load-bearing one — it is
  what makes the leak show up as a *smaller charge*. If the test passes with that seed deleted, it is
  not testing this ticket. Say so in the test comment.
- **Derive the expected gross from the requirement, not from a run.** Name the constants and compute
  the expected total in the test from the rule, so an assertion written by observing the code cannot
  bless the defect.

#### AMEND 3 — the price arm is under-tested

The draft's §2 correctly routes both `resolveTicketTypePrice` and `resolveTicketTypeFees`, but §4's
money fixture only exercises **fees**. TKT-237 gave **price rules** the channel axis, so a public
caller naming a reseller channel could move the **base price** — a more direct leak than the fee one.
Add a case: a channel-specific price rule exists; a public sale is refused / prices on the public
rule; assert the **resolved unit amount**, not just the fee basis.

#### AMEND 4 — one predicate, one test

The public guard has two distinct refusal reasons that must not short-circuit each other into a
single case: (a) the **schema** refuses an unknown property; (b) the **handler** refuses a non-nil
channel when `scope == nil`. A test that only posts through the gateway proves (a) and is silent
about (b) — deleting the handler check would stay green. Exercise (b) at the handler tier directly,
as `channel_seam_test.go` already does with its stub.

#### REJECT — §4's replacement of `TestAChannelledGASaleDoesNotYetForwardItsChannel`

The draft proposes replacing it. **Do not replace it; add beside it.** That test is inside the
tripwire file whose header says the assertions must not be deleted to make a build green. Under
option A the *scenario* it describes (a public GA sale naming a channel) becomes impossible, so the
honest edit is to convert it into the refusal assertion **in place, keeping its name's intent and its
comment history**, and to leave the two other tests in that file untouched. The distinction matters
because the file is the repo's record of why TKT-240 was reverted; a replacement loses that.

#### Pre-mortem — how this ships and is still wrong

1. **The 400 is asserted, the money is not.** A refusal-only test suite passes while an `absorbed`
   rule still under-charges through some path nobody enumerated. The money assertions in AMEND 2/3
   are the mitigation.
2. **`make check-generate` fails the gate** because regenerated `openapi_gen.go` /
   `commerce-api-types.gen.ts` were not committed before the run. ADR-009; the draft's §7 has the
   order right — follow it exactly.
3. **The storefront's generated type loses a field it never used.** Verify nothing in `web/` breaks
   at typecheck; `grep` says it does not, but the TS build is the proof.
4. **The partner path regresses silently.** Everything here is about removing a public capability;
   the partner tests are what prove nothing else moved. Run them explicitly.

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

1. **Dropping §3's legacy-replay branch in favour of pinning the 409 as accepted behaviour**
   (AMEND 1). This is a deliberate acceptance of a backward-compatibility edge, argued above; it is
   the most consequential thing in this critique and it is mine alone.
2. **The price-arm test case** (AMEND 3).
3. **Converting rather than replacing the tripwire test** (REJECT).

Named again at the Gate 2 hand-off.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan final — delta on the `kind=plan` draft

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended by the critique is the plan.** Not restated; read the three
together.

#### Decisions

1. **Legacy replay: accept the 409, do not add a branch. — TAKEN BY THE OWNER**, not by the agent.
   Raised explicitly because it is a backward-compatibility acceptance on a money path. `sameChannel`
   stays exact; a channel-less retry of a pre-change channelled public reservation gets a 409 and the
   caller's remedy is a new idempotency key. Pinned by a test asserting the 409 as **accepted
   behaviour** (the ADR-021 idiom: pin the gap so the claim cannot drift), and recorded in ADR-060 as
   a consequence. Rationale that decided it: the draft's predicate for "legacy" —
   `channel_code IS NOT NULL AND reseller_id IS NULL` — is *also* the shape of a row
   `exchange_target_test.go:106` calls "legal and routine", so it cannot distinguish what it claims,
   and a 409 refuses rather than mischarging.
2. **Convert the tripwire test in place; do not replace it** (critique REJECT). It is the repo's
   record of why TKT-240 was reverted.
3. **Test the price arm, not just fees** (AMEND 3) — TKT-237 gave price rules the channel axis, so
   the base price is reachable too.
4. **One predicate, one test** (AMEND 4) — the schema refusal and the handler refusal are separate
   mechanisms and each needs a case that can see it alone.
5. **Money assertions derived from the requirement** (AMEND 2), never from a run.

#### Scope (superseding the draft's file list where they differ)

| file | why |
|---|---|
| `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` | remove `channel_code` from `ReservationCreate`; `maxProperties` 4→3; keep `not:` and `additionalProperties:false`; rewrite the stale "known open defect" prose |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` | regenerated (ADR-009) |
| `web/storefront/src/lib/commerce-api-types.gen.ts` | regenerated |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` | handler refusal when `scope == nil`; fix the stale TKT-247 pointer at :535-538; update the `reserveRequest.ChannelCode` prose |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/channel_seam_test.go` | convert the channelled-GA test to the refusal boundary **in place**; fix the "See TKT-247" pointer |
| `smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go` | narrow the PUBLIC half only; partner half untouched; header gets the exact rationale sentence |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/catalog_fees_test.go` | contract-shape cases; the money fixture (fees, absorbed vs passed_on) |
| new: price-arm case | a channel-specific price rule must not price a public sale |
| new: legacy-replay case | the 409, asserted as accepted behaviour |
| `docs/adr/ADR-060-public-reservation-channel-entitlement.md` | the decision |

description:
**The half of the channel seam TKT-246 deliberately did not close, recorded so it is a
decision rather than an oversight.**

`POST /reservations` is unauthenticated and takes `channel_code` from the request body. That value
reaches **catalog's fee resolution** — so a public buyer naming `reseller-acme` is priced under that
channel's fee rules — and TKT-246 deliberately stops it from reaching **inventory**, so the sale
consumes PUBLIC stock.

TKT-246 could not close this half. Forwarding a body-supplied channel from an unauthenticated route
is the bypass TKT-240 was reverted for, and binding allocations to a seller does not rescue it
because an unbound allocation admits anyone and **every allocation in existence is unbound**. The
residual is therefore a **fee-attribution** defect, not an inventory-theft one: moving inventory now
requires a credential.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A public sale cannot be priced under a channel it is not entitled to. The likely shape is that
  channel-scoped fee/price rules require the same authorization inventory now requires — which makes
  this catalog's version of the ADR-024 question, not a repeat of it.
- Whatever is chosen, the ADR says which channels a public caller may name and why. "Any string"
  is a valid answer if it is argued: the registry is a lookup, not a constraint (ADR-024/TKT-235),
  and a channel code is not a secret.
- A test executes a public sale naming a reseller channel and asserts the resulting fee basis.

Parent: TKT-17. Non-goals: re-opening TKT-246's inventory decision; the seated seam (TKT-176).

objective.note: A public, unauthenticated caller names any channel_code in POST /reservations; it reaches catalog fee resolution and prices the sale under that channel's rules. Shaping upgraded the severity: because ADR-046 3 makes incidence load-bearing, a reseller rule with incidence=absorbed means the buyer is CHARGED LESS and the organizer eats the difference. This is a revenue-leak path, not only mis-attribution as the ticket text implies.

scope.note: IN: who may name a channel for FEE/PRICE resolution on the public reserve path, the ADR that records it, and a test executing a public sale naming a reseller channel. OUT (explicit non-goals, unchanged): TKT-246's inventory decision, the seated seam (TKT-176). Also OUT: the partner route, which is already correct - it takes the channel from its credential and overwrites any body value (server.go:630, ADR-056).

uncertainties.note: The unknown is a DECISION, not an investigation, so it is carried on `approach` with owner=human rather than a spike. Everything else resolved by reading: the two call sites, the incidence semantics, and the fact that catalog's resolve endpoint is public by design and deliberately hides other channels' rules from `candidates` (openapi.yaml:970-985).

dependencies.note: No open blockers. TKT-246 (Done) is the parent decision; TKT-240 (reverted) is the cautionary precedent. Nothing is blocked-by anything.

approach.note: DECIDED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-17: option A - public callers may name NO channel; channel_code becomes partner-only, taken from the credential and never from a body. Sent with a body channel, the public path answers 400 (contract refuses the field AND the handler refuses it, mirroring server.go:630's two-lines-of-defence reasoning). SCOPED DELIBERATELY: this is an AUTHORIZATION change, not a registry change. The channels registry stays a LOOKUP, not a constraint - no registry read is added to any sale path, so ADR-024/TKT-235/TKT-241 are NOT overturned. The partner half of smoke/channel_registry_lookup_test.go keeps proving an unregistered code sells verbatim; only the public half narrows, because a public sale can no longer name a channel at all.

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice once the human picks A, B or C: one eligibility rule in catalog's fee/price resolution, one ADR, one executing test. Under (B) it also needs one migration plus a registry field. No slicing needed beyond that.

success.note: The ticket's three COS are concrete and testable as written. Shaping adds the assertion that makes the third one bite: the test must assert the resulting FEE BASIS and the AMOUNT CHARGED, not merely that the request was refused - under incidence=absorbed the leak shows up as a smaller charge, and a refusal-only assertion is blind to it.

binding.rule: Making a request field load-bearing is an AUTHORIZATION change, not plumbing. Enumerate every producer of the value and ask which are authenticated. This ticket IS that rule's open case - TKT-240 was reverted for exactly it.
A guard with N predicates needs N tests, and a green test can assert the DEFECT as correct. Derive the expected fee basis from the requirement, never from a run.

governingAdrs.why: Channel allocations and the seller binding (`sold_by`, TKT-246 amendment). Says WHY inventory's guard sits under the pool row lock, which is exactly why that shape does not transfer to a fee read.
Fee rules representation. 3 (incidence: passed_on vs absorbed) is the clause that makes this a money defect; 4 fixes channel_code as an exact opaque string - no normalisation, no case folding.
Partner credential identity - file is ADR-056-partner-credential-identity.md. The precedent for a channel taken from a credential and never from a body.
Per-channel sales windows - the other axis keyed on channel_code.

Presale unlock codes (file: ADR-055-presale-unlock-codes.md) - the requires_code shape, and the source of the lookup-not-constraint principle the COS invokes. NOTE: ADR-055 is a DUPLICATED number - ADR-055-on-sale-write-rate-limiting.md also exists. Cite by filename.
Catalog organizer assertion - the existing catalog-side identity mechanism.

governingTests.why: A LIVE TRIPWIRE carrying an explicit instruction not to delete it. It pins the public GA hold as channel-free. A plan that 'fixes' this ticket by forwarding the channel fails here loudly - which is correct and intended. This ticket must NOT invert it: the inventory half is TKT-246's closed decision. STALE POINTER FOUND AT SHAPING: its closing comment says 'See TKT-247 for the remainder', but TKT-247 is a scanner-device flake. The remainder is THIS ticket, TKT-248. Fix that comment as part of this work.

Pins the commerce->catalog fee call, including that catalog is asked `channel_code=reseller` (line 321) and the request-field ceiling (line 413). Any eligibility change has to keep this contract honest or update it deliberately.
Pins fee_rules.channel_code at the store tier - the tier the mechanism actually lives at.

reference.summary: The seam is documented in prose at services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:362-382 (reserveRequest.ChannelCode) - read it first; it states the whole history including why TKT-240 was reverted.

The partner path already does the right thing: server.go:620-636 overwrites any body channel with the credential's, and refuses a mismatched organizer rather than silently rewriting it. Whatever is chosen for the public path should not disturb this.

catalog openapi.yaml:970-985 - resolveTicketTypePrice/Fees channel_code is public, omitting it is the public context and NOT a wildcard, and rules of other channels are hidden from `candidates` on purpose. The endpoint being public is a decision, not an oversight.
